title: Lower tail vanishing for complexes unbounded below
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension inside a fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$, and let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. Let $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\underline\Lambda$ be the pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaf [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})=D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ of its module sheaves [sk-def-sfb-module-objects; def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ for the constructible module sheaves: locally on affine opens of $X$ there is a finite stratification by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification] on each of which the restriction has a finite constant local model [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Write $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ for filtered colimits of these sheaves, computed in $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$, and $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ whose cohomology sheaves belong to $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$. Let $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, placed in degree zero, and fix a uniform Ext bound $d_C\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, meaning that $\Ext^r(C,N)=0$ for every $r>d_C$ and every $N\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, with Ext taken in the ambient derived category [def-pc-ext]. If $L\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ satisfies $H^q(L)=0$ for every $q>-d_C-1$, with no lower bound on its cohomology, then $\Hom_{D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})}(C,L)=0$.

external.place: *Milnor sequence.* Applying $\Hom(C,-)$, which takes products to products, to the defining triangle gives a long exact sequence whose relevant part is $$ \prod_n\Hom(C,L_n[-1])\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod_n\Hom(C,L_n[-1])\to\Hom(C,L)\to \prod_n\Hom(C,L_n)\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod_n\Hom(C,L_n), $$ i.e. $0\to\varprojlim^1_n\Hom(C,L_n[-1])\to\Hom(C,L)\to\varprojlim_n\Hom(C,L_n)\to0$.

proof.text: Choose a complex representing $L$ and set $L_n=\tau_{\geq-n}L$ for $n\in\mathbf N$, with the canonical maps $t_n:L_{n+1}\to L_n$. By [det-pe-left-complete-iso], applied with the sheaf of rings $\mathcal R=\Lambda_X$, the cone fibre of $1-T$ on $P=\prod_nL_n$ is isomorphic to $L$, where the $n$th component of $T$ is $t_n\circ\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$. Thus there is a distinguished triangle $L\to P\xrightarrow{1-T}P\to L[1]$. The termwise products used here are products in the derived category by [det-pe-products-derived]; the triangle is the shifted and rotated cone triangle in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No assertion that the product belongs to $\Dic$ is needed.

Apply the exactness of representable Hom on distinguished triangles [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], including its rotations, to the triangle of Step 1. The product universal property gives $\Hom(C,P)=\prod_n\Hom(C,L_n)$. Since the shift is an equivalence it preserves this product as well: composing with the projections identifies $\Hom(C,P[-1])$ with $\prod_n\Hom(C,L_n[-1])$. Put $G_n=\Hom(C,L_n[-1])$. We obtain the exact segment
$$\prod_nG_n\xrightarrow{1-t}\prod_nG_n\longrightarrow\Hom(C,L)\longrightarrow\prod_n\Hom(C,L_n).$$
Here $(1-t)(x)_n=x_n-t_n[-1]\circ x_{n+1}$: the formula follows by composing with the $n$th product projection. Thus it suffices to show that the last product is zero and $1-t$ on the first product is surjective; no separate theorem about $\varprojlim^1$ is being assumed.

The canonical truncation formulas [def-kun-truncations] give $H^q(L_n)=0$ for $q<-n$ and $H^q(L_n)=H^q(L)$ for $q\geq-n$. Thus every cohomology sheaf of $L_n$ is either zero or a cohomology sheaf of $L$, and belongs to $\IndCons$; hence $L_n\in\Dic$ by its definition. It is bounded with support in $[-n,-d_C-1]$ (the range may be empty). The bounded lower-tail theorem [det-finite-window-bounded], with the given uniform bound $d_C$, therefore gives $\Hom(C,L_n)=0$ for every $n$. Consequently the last product in Step 2 is zero.

For each $n\geq0$, apply [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] to $K=L_{n+1}$ with $b=-n$. This gives $\tau_{\leq-n-1}L_{n+1}\to L_{n+1}\to L_n\to$. The truncation formulas [def-kun-truncations] identify its first term with $H^{-n-1}(L)[n+1]$: it is supported only in degree $-n-1$, where its term is $\ker(d^{-n-1}:\operatorname{coker}d^{-n-2}\to L^{-n})=H^{-n-1}(L)$. The second truncation $\tau_{\geq-n}L_{n+1}$ is canonically $L_n$, with its canonical quotient map. Shift the triangle by $[-1]$ and use representable Hom exactness [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact]. With $B_n=H^{-n-1}(L)$ this yields
$$\Hom(C,B_n[n])\longrightarrow G_{n+1}\longrightarrow G_n\longrightarrow\Hom(C,B_n[n+1]).$$
Here $B_n\in\IndCons$ by the definition of $\Dic$. If $n>d_C$, the bounded objects $B_n[n]$ and $B_n[n+1]$ belong to $\Dic$ and are supported in degrees $-n$ and $-n-1$, respectively. Both degrees are at most $-d_C-1$, so [det-finite-window-bounded] gives zero for both outer groups. This is exactly the pair of Ext vanishings $\Ext^n(C,B_n)=\Ext^{n+1}(C,B_n)=0$ of the blueprint, obtained here as the single-cohomology special cases of the already cited bounded theorem. Exactness says that $G_{n+1}\to G_n$ is both injective and surjective.

proof.text: Write $u_n:G_{n+1}\to G_n$ for the maps of Step 4 and choose the natural number $N=d_C+1$. For an arbitrary $y=(y_n)\in\prod_nG_n$, define $x_N=0$ and, recursively for $n\geq N$, define $x_{n+1}=u_n^{-1}(x_n-y_n)$, which exists since $n>d_C$. For $n=N-1,N-2,\ldots,0$, recursively define $x_n=y_n+u_n(x_{n+1})$. These formulas give $x_n-u_n(x_{n+1})=y_n$ at every index, proving surjectivity of $1-t$. This is a direct calculation in abelian groups, including all finitely many transition maps that need not be invertible.

proof.text: In the exact segment of Step 2, the first arrow is surjective by Step 5 and the last term is zero by Step 3. For $f\in\Hom(C,L)$, exactness at $\Hom(C,L)$ lifts $f$ to $g\in\prod_nG_n$; surjectivity writes $g=(1-t)x$, whose image is zero by exactness. Thus $f=0$, as required.
